form.label: IoT Segmentation: Smart-Home Network Overview
form.description: Device behaviour, detections and firewall evidence for the segmented smart-home network. Counters and charts follow all filters; the severity filter applies to the detection panels only.

search.query: `iot_detections` | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | where sev_num >= $min_sev$
| inputlookup iot_captures | eval label=capture." (state ".state.", ".start_local.")" | sort start | table capture label
| inputlookup iot_devices | where role!="controller" | sort role device | table device

html.p: The smart-home devices live on their own network segment (the IoT network), separated from the household's computers (the main network). Their traffic was recorded at the router before and after the separation, together with the router's firewall log and the Pi-hole DNS log. Each recording is one capture; the configuration that was live is its state (A = one flat network … E = final, router locked down).
Severity: CRITICAL HIGH MEDIUM LOW INFO Simulated attacks come from a test host standing in for a compromised device; switch them off with the filter above.

tr.td: Every planned test scenario was run
At least 3 suspicious behaviours detected by transparent rules
Unauthorised access between the networks is blocked
Do the devices still work; function checklist 28/28 (E110)
Every result backed by reproducible evidence

html.p: Status from analysis.md §9. The evidence IDs (E01 … E111) are listed in evidence_manifest.md.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:conn device_role=iot | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats dc(device) AS devices
| inputlookup iot_captures | where "$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$" | stats count
`iot_index` | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats count
| stats sum(count) AS findings dc(rule) AS rules | fields findings
| where sev_num >= 4 | stats sum(count) AS n

`iot_index` sourcetype=iot:fw action=blocked | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats count

html.p: Everything the transparent rules flagged. Each row of the detail table says in plain words what happened.

search.query: | stats sum(count) AS count BY severity
| chart sum(count) AS count over rule_short by severity
| chart sum(count) AS count over device by severity | addtotals | sort - Total | fields - Total | head 10

chart.title: Detections per recording
chart.description: Which recording each finding comes from (state in brackets). "(no recording)" = firewall log only, e.g. the active tests.

search.query: | lookup iot_captures capture OUTPUT state start | eval recording=if(isnull(state), capture, capture." (".state.")") | chart sum(count) AS count over recording by severity | sort recording

chart.title: Real devices vs simulated attacks
chart.description: Simulated = the test host playing a compromised device.

search.query: | chart sum(count) AS count over origin by severity

table.title: Detection details
table.description: Highest severity first. Click a column header to sort.

search.query: | sort - sev_num - count | eval When=strftime(_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | rename severity AS Severity, rule_label AS Rule, detail AS "What happened", device AS Device, origin AS Source, capture AS Recording, count AS Count | table When Severity Rule "What happened" Device Source Recording Count

html.h2: What is normal for each device
html.p: The baseline: who each device talks to and how much. Rules R1, R3, R5 and R9 compare new traffic with the baseline recordings.

chart.title: Internet upload per device (bytes per hour, log scale)
chart.description: Data each device sent to the internet. Spikes are uploads; flat lines are routine check-ins.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:volume | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | timechart span=1h sum(out_wan) BY device
`iot_index` sourcetype=iot:annotation | eval annotation_label=label.": ".text, annotation_category=kind

chart.title: Who each device talks to (share of its traffic)
chart.description: By bytes. "Local discovery" is multicast that never leaves the house.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:conn | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | `iot_peer_label` | eval bytes=bytes_out+bytes_in | chart sum(bytes) over device by talks_to

table.title: Device profiles
table.description: One line per device: its normal footprint. "Started by others" are connections a controller or another host opened to the device.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:conn | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats dc(eval(if(peer_class="wan", peer_ip, null()))) AS internet_servers count AS connections count(eval(initiated_by="peer")) AS started_by_others values(capture) AS recordings BY device device_mac device_role | join type=left device [ search `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:volume | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | bin _time span=1h | stats sum(out_wan) AS up sum(in_wan) AS down BY _time device | stats median(up) AS med_up median(down) AS med_down BY device ] | join type=left device [ search `iot_index` (sourcetype=iot:pihole OR sourcetype=iot:dns) | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats dc(query) AS domains BY device ] | lookup iot_devices mac AS device_mac OUTPUT type local_only baselined | eval up_txt=if(isnull(med_up), "none", round(med_up/1000, 1)." kB"), down_txt=if(isnull(med_down), "none", round(med_down/1000, 1)." kB") | eval Recordings=mvjoin(recordings, ", "), lo=if(local_only="true", "yes", "no"), Baselined=if(baselined="true", "yes", "no") | fillnull value=0 domains | rename device AS Device, type AS Type, internet_servers AS "Internet servers", domains AS "Domains looked up", connections AS Connections, started_by_others AS "Started by others", device_role AS Role, up_txt AS "Internet upload / h (median)", down_txt AS "Internet download / h (median)", lo AS "Local only" | table Device Type Role "Local only" Baselined "Internet servers" "Domains looked up" "Internet upload / h (median)" "Internet download / h (median)" Connections "Started by others" Recordings

html.p: What the router's firewall stopped, and who could reach the devices before and after the separation.

chart.title: What the firewall did
chart.description: Logged = allowed but recorded. Blocked and redirected = stopped at the boundary. Log scale.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:fw | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | `iot_fw_label` | eval origin=case(device_role="iot", "Real device", device_role="test", "Test host", true(), "Other host") | chart count over what by origin

chart.title: Hosts that started connections to IoT devices
chart.description: Before the separation (state A) many household hosts reached the devices; afterwards only the controllers.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:conn initiated_by=peer | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | `iot_peer_label` | eval recording=capture." (".state.")" | chart dc(peer_ip) AS hosts over recording by talks_to

table.title: Blocked attempts by destination
table.description: Every blocked or redirected attempt from the IoT side, grouped by target.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:fw action!=logged | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | `iot_fw_label` | fillnull value="" dest_name | eval Destination=if(dest_name!="", dest_name." (".dest_ip.")", dest_ip), port=coalesce(dest_port, "-") | stats count AS Attempts values(port) AS Ports min(_time) AS first max(_time) AS last BY device device_role what Destination | eval Ports=mvjoin(mvindex(Ports, 0, 7), ", ").if(mvcount(Ports)>8, " …", ""), first_txt=strftime(first, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), last_txt=strftime(last, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | sort - Attempts | rename device AS Device, device_role AS Role, what AS What, first_txt AS "First seen", last_txt AS "Last seen" | table Device Role What Destination Ports Attempts "First seen" "Last seen"

html.p: Controllers (HomePod, iPhone, Mac) reach the devices over Matter (UDP 5540), and the devices get their DNS answers from Pi-hole. The full 28-point function checklist passed in the final state (evidence E110, E111).

chart.title: Controller sessions per device (Matter)
chart.description: Matter connections a controller opened to each device, across the selected recordings.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:conn initiated_by=peer (dest_port=5540 OR src_port=5540) | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | eval controller=if(isnull(peer_name) OR peer_name="", peer_ip, peer_name) | chart count over device by controller

chart.title: DNS answers for the devices (Pi-hole)
chart.description: Blocked lookups are telemetry domains on the block list, e.g. the Hue diagnostics host.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:pihole | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | eval answer=if(blocked="true", "Blocked (tracking / telemetry)", "Answered") | chart count over device by answer

html.p: What the evidence covers: the recordings, the operator's notes and the health of the capture.

search.query: | inputlookup iot_captures | where "$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$" | eval Baseline=if(baseline="true", "yes", "no"), Hours=round((end-start)/3600, 1) | rename capture AS Recording, state AS State, start_local AS Start, end_local AS End, description AS "What it is" | table Recording State Baseline Start End Hours "What it is"

`iot_index` sourcetype=iot:annotation | where "$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$" OR isnull(capture) OR capture="" | sort _time | eval When=strftime(_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | rename kind AS Kind, label AS What, text AS Details, capture AS Recording | table When Recording Kind What Details

chart.title: IPv6 router advertisements (capture health, R11)
chart.description: About 7 per minute is normal. A run of zeros during a recording means the router stopped advertising IPv6.

search.query: `iot_index` sourcetype=iot:health | where "$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$" | timechart span=5m sum(router_adverts) BY iface
`iot_index` sourcetype=iot:annotation | eval annotation_label=label.": ".text, annotation_category=kind

table.title: Events per data source
table.description: Totals should match pipeline_out/prepare_report.json when no filter is set.

search.query: `iot_index` | where ("$cap$"="__all" OR capture="$cap$") AND ("$dev$"="__all" OR device="$dev$") AND ("$tests$"="yes" OR isnull(device_role) OR device_role!="test") | stats count BY sourcetype | eval Source=case(sourcetype="iot:conn", "Connections (Zeek)", sourcetype="iot:dns", "DNS on the wire (Zeek)", sourcetype="iot:tls", "TLS sessions (Zeek)", sourcetype="iot:tls_hello", "TLS fingerprints (tshark)", sourcetype="iot:http", "Plain HTTP (Zeek)", sourcetype="iot:dhcp", "DHCP (Zeek)", sourcetype="iot:volume", "Volume per device-minute (pcap)", sourcetype="iot:health", "Capture health per minute (pcap)", sourcetype="iot:fw", "Router firewall log", sourcetype="iot:pihole", "Pi-hole DNS log", sourcetype="iot:annotation", "Operator notes", true(), sourcetype) | rename sourcetype AS Sourcetype, count AS Events | table Source Sourcetype Events

html.p: Each rule is one plain condition with a fixed threshold, so anyone can check why it fired. Full definitions: analysis.md §8; one-line versions: results_to_evidence.md. The searches are the macros iot_det_r1 … iot_det_r12, iot_det_fw, iot_det_dev in this app.

tr.td: a domain the device never looked up during a baseline recording
Tried to reach the main network
blocked by the firewall; info when it is a Matter status message to a controller (policy, rec. 22)
more than 10x the device's normal hourly internet traffic (floor 10 kB/h, rec. 20); severity grows with the ratio
sent to an address that cannot exist on the internet (e.g. the SwitchBot leak to 255.2.0.0)
blocked DNS lookups per hour above 5x the first baseline
more than 10 new connections to one internet server within 10 minutes
Asked a DNS server other than Pi-hole
high if it reached an outside resolver, medium if the router redirected it to Pi-hole
Local-only device talked to the internet
a device marked local_only (the Matter switches) contacted the internet
a TLS client fingerprint (JA4) not seen during a baseline: new software or a reboot
Unencrypted web traffic to the internet
plain HTTP to the internet: anyone on the path can read it
no IPv6 router advertisement for 3 minutes or more during a recording
an IoT-side host tried a router service it may not use (state E hardening)
Unexpected device on the IoT network
a device not in the inventory, a controller or a personal device joined the IoT segment
